commit_message:
mqtt: free any leftover when done

Oss-fuzz found an issue when the "sendleftovers" pointer could leak memory.
Fix this by always freeing it (if still assigned) in the done function.

Bug: https://bugs.chromium.org/p/oss-fuzz/issues/detail?id=43515
Closes #8274

fix_commit_message:
mqtt: convert sendleftovers to dynbuf

Avoid frequent strdups/free calls, including the double-free risk.

Reported-by: Ronald Crane
Closes #16823
agent_reasoning: Without this change, mqtt_doing() captures `mq->sendleftovers` into a local `ptr`, calls mqtt_send(data, ptr, ...), and unconditionally frees `ptr` afterward. mqtt_send() only rewrites `mq->sendleftovers`/`mq->nsend` on the full-send or partial-send-with-successful-memdup paths; if Curl_memdup() returns NULL (OOM) it returns CURLE_OUT_OF_MEMORY while `mq->sendleftovers` still references the original (soon to be double-freed) allocation. mqtt_doing() then frees `ptr` (the same address), so `mq->sendleftovers` becomes a dangling pointer rather than NULL. Because mqtt_done() (added to free any leftover at completion) also calls Curl_safefree(mq->sendleftovers), the dangling pointer gets freed a second time — a double-free reachable via a transfer that experiences a short write followed by an allocation failure, matching the oss-fuzz report. The fix detaches `mq->sendleftovers`/`mq->nsend` (setting them to NULL/0) before the retry call, so mqtt_send() can only ever leave `mq->sendleftovers` as NULL or a newly, distinctly allocated buffer — never the same pointer that mqtt_doing() is about to free — eliminating the double-free while preserving normal send/retry behavior.
